text.what: A gravel terrace at the south end of the North Island, in the rain shadow of the Tararua Range, with a town laid out as a Union Jack. Small, dry, windy, and planted almost entirely to pinot noir.

kin.as: The reason the terrace was planted at all.
The country's other pinot argument, 900 km south.
Propagated here first, and named for the customs officer.
